text_blocks.snippet: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a bacterial infection of the colon, causing diarrhea and potentially severe inflammation (colitis). It is often associated with antibiotic use, which disrupts the gut's natural bacterial balance. CDI can range from mild diarrhea to severe, life-threatening complications.
snippet_highlighted_words: a bacterial infection of the colon, causing diarrhea and potentially severe inflammation (colitis)

list.title: Cause:
list.snippet: CDI is caused by the bacterium Clostridioides difficile (formerly Clostridium difficile), which produces toxins that damage the colon.

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: Antibiotic use, particularly certain types like clindamycin, cephalosporins, and quinolones, is a major risk factor. Other risk factors include older age, weakened immune systems, hospitalization, and living in long-term care facilities.
